Risks to watch: litigation, integration and regulatory pressure
---------------------------------------------------------------

While the long‑term fundamentals appear solid, ABT is **not risk‑free**.

### 1. Deal execution and integration

The Exact Sciences acquisition must clear **regulatory and shareholder approvals**, and Abbott will then need to integrate a fast‑growing, R&D‑intensive oncology business without disrupting its culture or pipeline. Analysts note that **delays, divestiture requirements or integration missteps** could erode the high‑teens growth that makes Exact so attractive in the first place. [[35]](https://www.stocktitan.net/news/ABT/abbott-to-acquire-exact-sciences-a-leader-in-large-and-fast-growing-pvbv6z5xtczh.html?utm_source=ts2.tech)

### 2. Product safety and brand reputation

The Libre 3 correction underscores Abbott’s exposure to **device quality and safety risks**. Regulators have been tightening scrutiny on CGM systems, and any escalation — such as an FDA‑logged recall or more severe adverse‑event data — could pressure Libre’s growth and open the door wider for competitors. [[36]](https://www.medtechdive.com/news/abbott-libre-3-correction-accuracy/806345/?utm_source=ts2.tech)

### 3. Ongoing NEC baby formula litigation

Abbott also faces continuing **legal overhang** from lawsuits alleging that its **Similac** products contributed to **necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC)** in premature infants. A November 4, 2025 update from a plaintiffs’ law firm notes that around **755 cases remain pending in the federal MDL** (MDL 3026) alongside additional state‑court filings, with some early jury verdicts in related cases against other manufacturers reaching very large sums. [[37]](https://www.lawsuit-information-center.com/nec-baby-formula-lawsuits.html?utm_source=ts2.tech)

While allegations and verdicts are subject to appeals and do not automatically translate to Abbott outcomes, the litigation adds uncertainty around **potential future settlements, legal expenses and reputational impact**.

### 4. Macro and pricing pressures

Finally, Abbott is exposed to broader issues such as: [[38]](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/abbott-reports-third-quarter-2025-results-and-reaffirms-full-year-guidance-302584746.html?utm_source=ts2.tech)

*   **Foreign‑exchange volatility**, which can drag on reported international sales
*   **Volume‑based procurement and pricing reforms**, especially in China, affecting diagnostics
*   **Hospital capital‑spending cycles**, which can impact device orders and lab equipment upgrades

Management highlighted some of these pressures in explaining Q3 performance, even as it reaffirmed full‑year guidance.

Abbott Laboratories, together with its subsidiaries, discovers, develops, manufactures, and sells health care products worldwide. It operates in four segments: Established Pharmaceutical Products, Diagnostic Products, Nutritional Products, and Medical Devices. The company provides generic pharmaceuticals for the treatment of pancreatic exocrine insufficiency, irritable bowel syndrome or biliary spasm, intrahepatic cholestasis or depressive symptoms, gynecological disorder, hormone replacement therapy, dyslipidemia, hypertension, hypothyroidism, hypertriglyceridemia, Ménière's disease and vestibular vertigo, pain, fever, inflammation, and migraine, as well as provides anti-infective clarithromycin, influenza vaccine, and products to regulate physiological rhythm of the colon. It also offers laboratory and transfusion medicine systems in the areas of immunoassay, clinical chemistry, hematology, and transfusion serology testing; molecular diagnostics polymerase chain reaction instrument systems that automate the extraction, purification, and preparation of DNA and RNA from patient samples, and detect and measure infectious agents; point of care systems; cartridges for testing blood gas, chemistry, electrolytes, coagulation, and immunoassay; rapid diagnostics lateral flow testing products; molecular point-of-care testing for HIV, SARS-CoV-2, influenza A and B, RSV, and strep A; cardiometabolic test systems; and drug and alcohol test. In addition, the company provides pediatric and adult nutritional products and infant formula; rhythm management, electrophysiology, heart failure, vascular, and structural heart devices for the treatment of cardiovascular diseases; diabetes care products, such as glucose and blood glucose monitoring systems; and neuromodulation devices for the management of chronic pain and movement disorders. Abbott Laboratories was founded in 1888 and is based in North Chicago, Illinois.

# Q3 Earnings Outperformers: Abbott Laboratories (NYSE:ABT) And The Rest Of The Medical Devices & Supplies - Diversified Stocks

Adam Hejl

5 min read

In this article:  

[ABT

-0.72%](/quote/ABT/ "ABT")

Looking back on medical devices & supplies - diversified stocks’ Q3 earnings, we examine this quarter’s best and worst performers, including Abbott Laboratories (NYSE:ABT) and its peers.

The medical devices industry operates a business model that balances steady demand with significant investments in innovation and regulatory compliance. The industry benefits from recurring revenue streams tied to consumables, maintenance services, and incremental upgrades to the latest technologies. However, the capital-intensive nature of product development, coupled with lengthy regulatory pathways and the need for clinical validation, can weigh on profitability and timelines. In addition, there are constant pricing pressures from healthcare systems and insurers maximizing cost efficiency. Over the next several years, one tailwind is demographic–aging populations means rising chronic disease rates that drive greater demand for medical interventions and monitoring solutions. Advances in digital health, such as remote patient monitoring and smart devices, are also expected to unlock new demand by shortening upgrade cycles. On the other hand, the industry faces headwinds from pricing and reimbursement pressures as healthcare providers increasingly adopt value-based care models. Additionally, the integration of cybersecurity for connected devices adds further risk and complexity for device manufacturers.

The 5 medical devices & supplies - diversified stocks we track reported a mixed Q3. As a group, revenues beat analysts’ consensus estimates by 0.6% while next quarter’s revenue guidance was in line.

While some medical devices & supplies - diversified stocks have fared somewhat better than others, they have collectively declined. On average, share prices are down 4.3% since the latest earnings results.

## Abbott Laboratories (NYSE:ABT)

With roots dating back to 1888 when founder Dr. Wallace Abbott began producing precise, dosage-form medications, Abbott Laboratories (NYSE:ABT) develops and sells a diverse range of healthcare products including medical devices, diagnostics, nutrition products, and branded generic pharmaceuticals.

Abbott Laboratories reported revenues of $11.37 billion, up 6.9% year on year. This print was in line with analysts’ expectations, but overall, it was a mixed quarter for the company with organic revenue in line with analysts’ estimates.

"Our third-quarter results demonstrate our ability to deliver consistent, high-quality performance," said Robert B. Ford, chairman and chief executive officer, Abbott.

Unsurprisingly, the stock is down 7% since reporting and currently trades at $123.91.

## Best Q3: Neogen (NASDAQ:NEOG)

Founded in 1981 and operating at the intersection of food safety and animal health, Neogen (NASDAQ:NEOG) develops and manufactures diagnostic tests and related products to detect dangerous substances in food and pharmaceuticals for animal health.

Neogen reported revenues of $209.2 million, down 3.6% year on year, outperforming analysts’ expectations by 2.6%. The business had a very strong quarter with an impressive beat of analysts’ revenue estimates and full-year revenue guidance slightly topping analysts’ expectations.

Neogen achieved the biggest analyst estimates beat among its peers. The market seems happy with the results as the stock is up 7.9% since reporting. It currently trades at $6.28.

## Weakest Q3: Baxter (NYSE:BAX)

With a history dating back to 1931 and products used in over 100 countries, Baxter International (NYSE:BAX) provides essential healthcare products including dialysis therapies, IV solutions, infusion systems, surgical products, and patient monitoring technologies to hospitals and clinics worldwide.

Baxter reported revenues of $2.84 billion, up 5% year on year, falling short of analysts’ expectations by 1.4%. It was a softer quarter as it posted a significant miss of analysts’ full-year EPS guidance estimates and revenue guidance for next quarter missing analysts’ expectations significantly.

Baxter delivered the weakest performance against analyst estimates in the group. As expected, the stock is down 18.2% since the results and currently trades at $18.35.

Beyond today’s insider headline, the **dominant story** for ABT in late November is its move into cancer diagnostics through a huge M&A deal.

On **November 20, 2025**, Abbott announced a definitive agreement to acquire **Exact Sciences (NASDAQ: EXAS)**, a leading cancer screening and precision oncology company. Libre 3 sensor correction: safety and reputation in the spotlight
-----------------------------------------------------------------

A second important overhang is the **safety correction** affecting Abbott’s continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) products.

On **November 24, 2025**, MedTech Dive reported that Abbott issued a **“medical device correction”** — not a formal recall — for around **3 million FreeStyle Libre 3 and Libre 3 Plus sensors** in the United States. The move followed reports that some sensors may deliver **falsely low glucose readings**, potentially leading users to overtreat with carbohydrates or reduce insulin unnecessarily. [[18]](https://www.medtechdive.com/news/abbott-libre-3-correction-accuracy/806345/?utm_source=ts2.tech)

Key data from Abbott’s communication, as reported: [[19]](https://www.medtechdive.com/news/abbott-libre-3-correction-accuracy/806345/?utm_source=ts2.tech)

*   **736 severe adverse events** and **7 deaths** worldwide associated with the affected sensors
*   In the **U.S.**, **57 severe adverse events** and **no deaths**
*   The problem is tied to **a single manufacturing line**, and roughly half of the affected sensors have already been used or expired
*   Abbott is offering **free replacement sensors** and does **not expect major supply disruptions**

The U.S. FDA had not yet listed the correction in its recall database as of the latest reporting, but the situation is being closely followed by regulators, physicians and patient groups. [[20]](https://www.medtechdive.com/news/abbott-libre-3-correction-accuracy/806345/?utm_source=ts2.tech)

The **Libre franchise** has been one of Abbott’s fastest‑growing product lines within Medical Devices, competing directly with Dexcom and Insulet in the booming CGM market. Any perceived reliability issues could: [[21]](https://www.medtechdive.com/news/abbott-libre-3-correction-accuracy/806345/?utm_source=ts2.tech)

*   Slow new patient uptake
*   Increase warranty or replacement costs
*   Heighten regulatory scrutiny and potential litigation risk

So far, the company’s messaging emphasizes that it has isolated the manufacturing issue and is proactively replacing affected sensors, but investors will watch for **any escalation into a formal recall or further adverse event disclosures**.

Risks to watch: litigation, integration and regulatory pressure
---------------------------------------------------------------

While the long‑term fundamentals appear solid, ABT is **not risk‑free**.

### 1. Deal execution and integration

The Exact Sciences acquisition must clear **regulatory and shareholder approvals**, and Abbott will then need to integrate a fast‑growing, R&D‑intensive oncology business without disrupting its culture or pipeline. Analysts note that **delays, divestiture requirements or integration missteps** could erode the high‑teens growth that makes Exact so attractive in the first place. [[35]](https://www.stocktitan.net/news/ABT/abbott-to-acquire-exact-sciences-a-leader-in-large-and-fast-growing-pvbv6z5xtczh.html?utm_source=ts2.tech)

### 2. Product safety and brand reputation

The Libre 3 correction underscores Abbott’s exposure to **device quality and safety risks**. Regulators have been tightening scrutiny on CGM systems, and any escalation — such as an FDA‑logged recall or more severe adverse‑event data — could pressure Libre’s growth and open the door wider for competitors. [[36]](https://www.medtechdive.com/news/abbott-libre-3-correction-accuracy/806345/?utm_source=ts2.tech)

### 3. Ongoing NEC baby formula litigation

Abbott also faces continuing **legal overhang** from lawsuits alleging that its **Similac** products contributed to **necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC)** in premature infants. A November 4, 2025 update from a plaintiffs’ law firm notes that around **755 cases remain pending in the federal MDL** (MDL 3026) alongside additional state‑court filings, with some early jury verdicts in related cases against other manufacturers reaching very large sums. [[37]](https://www.lawsuit-information-center.com/nec-baby-formula-lawsuits.html?utm_source=ts2.tech)

While allegations and verdicts are subject to appeals and do not automatically translate to Abbott outcomes, the litigation adds uncertainty around **potential future settlements, legal expenses and reputational impact**.

### 4. Macro and pricing pressures

Finally, Abbott is exposed to broader issues such as: [[38]](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/abbott-reports-third-quarter-2025-results-and-reaffirms-full-year-guidance-302584746.html?utm_source=ts2.tech)

*   **Foreign‑exchange volatility**, which can drag on reported international sales
*   **Volume‑based procurement and pricing reforms**, especially in China, affecting diagnostics
*   **Hospital capital‑spending cycles**, which can impact device orders and lab equipment upgrades

Management highlighted some of these pressures in explaining Q3 performance, even as it reaffirmed full‑year guidance.

Abbott Laboratories, together with its subsidiaries, discovers, develops, manufactures, and sells health care products worldwide. It operates in four segments: Established Pharmaceutical Products, Diagnostic Products, Nutritional Products, and Medical Devices. The company provides generic pharmaceuticals for the treatment of pancreatic exocrine insufficiency, irritable bowel syndrome or biliary spasm, intrahepatic cholestasis or depressive symptoms, gynecological disorder, hormone replacement therapy, dyslipidemia, hypertension, hypothyroidism, hypertriglyceridemia, Ménière's disease and vestibular vertigo, pain, fever, inflammation, and migraine, as well as provides anti-infective clarithromycin, influenza vaccine, and products to regulate physiological rhythm of the colon. It also offers laboratory and transfusion medicine systems in the areas of immunoassay, clinical chemistry, hematology, and transfusion serology testing; molecular diagnostics polymerase chain reaction instrument systems that automate the extraction, purification, and preparation of DNA and RNA from patient samples, and detect and measure infectious agents; point of care systems; cartridges for testing blood gas, chemistry, electrolytes, coagulation, and immunoassay; rapid diagnostics lateral flow testing products; molecular point-of-care testing for HIV, SARS-CoV-2, influenza A and B, RSV, and strep A; cardiometabolic test systems; and drug and alcohol test. In addition, the company provides pediatric and adult nutritional products and infant formula; rhythm management, electrophysiology, heart failure, vascular, and structural heart devices for the treatment of cardiovascular diseases; diabetes care products, such as glucose and blood glucose monitoring systems; and neuromodulation devices for the management of chronic pain and movement disorders. Abbott Laboratories was founded in 1888 and is based in North Chicago, Illinois.

-----------------------------------------------------

On **November 20, 2025**, Abbott announced a definitive agreement to acquire **Exact Sciences (NASDAQ: EXAS)**, a leading cancer screening and precision oncology company. *   Expand Cologuard and other tests internationally
*   Defend the franchise as blood‑based screening options gain traction

Libre 3 sensor correction: safety and reputation in the spotlight
-----------------------------------------------------------------

A second important overhang is the **safety correction** affecting Abbott’s continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) products.

On **November 24, 2025**, MedTech Dive reported that Abbott issued a **“medical device correction”** — not a formal recall — for around **3 million FreeStyle Libre 3 and Libre 3 Plus sensors** in the United States. The move followed reports that some sensors may deliver **falsely low glucose readings**, potentially leading users to overtreat with carbohydrates or reduce insulin unnecessarily. [[18]](https://www.medtechdive.com/news/abbott-libre-3-correction-accuracy/806345/?utm_source=ts2.tech)

Key data from Abbott’s communication, as reported: [[19]](https://www.medtechdive.com/news/abbott-libre-3-correction-accuracy/806345/?utm_source=ts2.tech)

*   **736 severe adverse events** and **7 deaths** worldwide associated with the affected sensors
*   In the **U.S.**, **57 severe adverse events** and **no deaths**
*   The problem is tied to **a single manufacturing line**, and roughly half of the affected sensors have already been used or expired
*   Abbott is offering **free replacement sensors** and does **not expect major supply disruptions**

The U.S. FDA had not yet listed the correction in its recall database as of the latest reporting, but the situation is being closely followed by regulators, physicians and patient groups. [[20]](https://www.medtechdive.com/news/abbott-libre-3-correction-accuracy/806345/?utm_source=ts2.tech)

The **Libre franchise** has been one of Abbott’s fastest‑growing product lines within Medical Devices, competing directly with Dexcom and Insulet in the booming CGM market. Any perceived reliability issues could: [[21]](https://www.medtechdive.com/news/abbott-libre-3-correction-accuracy/806345/?utm_source=ts2.tech)

*   Slow new patient uptake
*   Increase warranty or replacement costs
*   Heighten regulatory scrutiny and potential litigation risk

So far, the company’s messaging emphasizes that it has isolated the manufacturing issue and is proactively replacing affected sensors, but investors will watch for **any escalation into a formal recall or further adverse event disclosures**.

Risks to watch: litigation, integration and regulatory pressure
---------------------------------------------------------------

While the long‑term fundamentals appear solid, ABT is **not risk‑free**.

### 1. Deal execution and integration

The Exact Sciences acquisition must clear **regulatory and shareholder approvals**, and Abbott will then need to integrate a fast‑growing, R&D‑intensive oncology business without disrupting its culture or pipeline. Analysts note that **delays, divestiture requirements or integration missteps** could erode the high‑teens growth that makes Exact so attractive in the first place. [[35]](https://www.stocktitan.net/news/ABT/abbott-to-acquire-exact-sciences-a-leader-in-large-and-fast-growing-pvbv6z5xtczh.html?utm_source=ts2.tech)

### 2. Product safety and brand reputation

The Libre 3 correction underscores Abbott’s exposure to **device quality and safety risks**. Regulators have been tightening scrutiny on CGM systems, and any escalation — such as an FDA‑logged recall or more severe adverse‑event data — could pressure Libre’s growth and open the door wider for competitors. [[36]](https://www.medtechdive.com/news/abbott-libre-3-correction-accuracy/806345/?utm_source=ts2.tech)

### 3. Ongoing NEC baby formula litigation

Abbott also faces continuing **legal overhang** from lawsuits alleging that its **Similac** products contributed to **necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC)** in premature infants. A November 4, 2025 update from a plaintiffs’ law firm notes that around **755 cases remain pending in the federal MDL** (MDL 3026) alongside additional state‑court filings, with some early jury verdicts in related cases against other manufacturers reaching very large sums. [[37]](https://www.lawsuit-information-center.com/nec-baby-formula-lawsuits.html?utm_source=ts2.tech)

While allegations and verdicts are subject to appeals and do not automatically translate to Abbott outcomes, the litigation adds uncertainty around **potential future settlements, legal expenses and reputational impact**.

### 4. Macro and pricing pressures

Finally, Abbott is exposed to broader issues such as: [[38]](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/abbott-reports-third-quarter-2025-results-and-reaffirms-full-year-guidance-302584746.html?utm_source=ts2.tech)

*   **Foreign‑exchange volatility**, which can drag on reported international sales
*   **Volume‑based procurement and pricing reforms**, especially in China, affecting diagnostics
*   **Hospital capital‑spending cycles**, which can impact device orders and lab equipment upgrades

Management highlighted some of these pressures in explaining Q3 performance, even as it reaffirmed full‑year guidance.

Abbott Laboratories, together with its subsidiaries, discovers, develops, manufactures, and sells health care products worldwide. It operates in four segments: Established Pharmaceutical Products, Diagnostic Products, Nutritional Products, and Medical Devices. The company provides generic pharmaceuticals for the treatment of pancreatic exocrine insufficiency, irritable bowel syndrome or biliary spasm, intrahepatic cholestasis or depressive symptoms, gynecological disorder, hormone replacement therapy, dyslipidemia, hypertension, hypothyroidism, hypertriglyceridemia, Ménière's disease and vestibular vertigo, pain, fever, inflammation, and migraine, as well as provides anti-infective clarithromycin, influenza vaccine, and products to regulate physiological rhythm of the colon. It also offers laboratory and transfusion medicine systems in the areas of immunoassay, clinical chemistry, hematology, and transfusion serology testing; molecular diagnostics polymerase chain reaction instrument systems that automate the extraction, purification, and preparation of DNA and RNA from patient samples, and detect and measure infectious agents; point of care systems; cartridges for testing blood gas, chemistry, electrolytes, coagulation, and immunoassay; rapid diagnostics lateral flow testing products; molecular point-of-care testing for HIV, SARS-CoV-2, influenza A and B, RSV, and strep A; cardiometabolic test systems; and drug and alcohol test. In addition, the company provides pediatric and adult nutritional products and infant formula; rhythm management, electrophysiology, heart failure, vascular, and structural heart devices for the treatment of cardiovascular diseases; diabetes care products, such as glucose and blood glucose monitoring systems; and neuromodulation devices for the management of chronic pain and movement disorders. Abbott Laboratories was founded in 1888 and is based in North Chicago, Illinois.

# Q3 Earnings Outperformers: Abbott Laboratories (NYSE:ABT) And The Rest Of The Medical Devices & Supplies - Diversified Stocks

Adam Hejl

5 min read

In this article:  

[ABT

-0.72%](/quote/ABT/ "ABT")

Looking back on medical devices & supplies - diversified stocks’ Q3 earnings, we examine this quarter’s best and worst performers, including Abbott Laboratories (NYSE:ABT) and its peers.

The medical devices industry operates a business model that balances steady demand with significant investments in innovation and regulatory compliance. The industry benefits from recurring revenue streams tied to consumables, maintenance services, and incremental upgrades to the latest technologies. However, the capital-intensive nature of product development, coupled with lengthy regulatory pathways and the need for clinical validation, can weigh on profitability and timelines. In addition, there are constant pricing pressures from healthcare systems and insurers maximizing cost efficiency. Over the next several years, one tailwind is demographic–aging populations means rising chronic disease rates that drive greater demand for medical interventions and monitoring solutions. Advances in digital health, such as remote patient monitoring and smart devices, are also expected to unlock new demand by shortening upgrade cycles. On the other hand, the industry faces headwinds from pricing and reimbursement pressures as healthcare providers increasingly adopt value-based care models. Additionally, the integration of cybersecurity for connected devices adds further risk and complexity for device manufacturers.

The 5 medical devices & supplies - diversified stocks we track reported a mixed Q3. As a group, revenues beat analysts’ consensus estimates by 0.6% while next quarter’s revenue guidance was in line.

While some medical devices & supplies - diversified stocks have fared somewhat better than others, they have collectively declined. On average, share prices are down 4.3% since the latest earnings results.

## Abbott Laboratories (NYSE:ABT)

With roots dating back to 1888 when founder Dr. Wallace Abbott began producing precise, dosage-form medications, Abbott Laboratories (NYSE:ABT) develops and sells a diverse range of healthcare products including medical devices, diagnostics, nutrition products, and branded generic pharmaceuticals.

Abbott Laboratories reported revenues of $11.37 billion, up 6.9% year on year. This print was in line with analysts’ expectations, but overall, it was a mixed quarter for the company with organic revenue in line with analysts’ estimates.

"Our third-quarter results demonstrate our ability to deliver consistent, high-quality performance," said Robert B. Ford, chairman and chief executive officer, Abbott.

Unsurprisingly, the stock is down 7% since reporting and currently trades at $123.91.

## Best Q3: Neogen (NASDAQ:NEOG)

Founded in 1981 and operating at the intersection of food safety and animal health, Neogen (NASDAQ:NEOG) develops and manufactures diagnostic tests and related products to detect dangerous substances in food and pharmaceuticals for animal health.

Neogen reported revenues of $209.2 million, down 3.6% year on year, outperforming analysts’ expectations by 2.6%. The business had a very strong quarter with an impressive beat of analysts’ revenue estimates and full-year revenue guidance slightly topping analysts’ expectations.

Neogen achieved the biggest analyst estimates beat among its peers. The market seems happy with the results as the stock is up 7.9% since reporting. It currently trades at $6.28.

## Weakest Q3: Baxter (NYSE:BAX)

With a history dating back to 1931 and products used in over 100 countries, Baxter International (NYSE:BAX) provides essential healthcare products including dialysis therapies, IV solutions, infusion systems, surgical products, and patient monitoring technologies to hospitals and clinics worldwide.

Baxter reported revenues of $2.84 billion, up 5% year on year, falling short of analysts’ expectations by 1.4%. It was a softer quarter as it posted a significant miss of analysts’ full-year EPS guidance estimates and revenue guidance for next quarter missing analysts’ expectations significantly.

Baxter delivered the weakest performance against analyst estimates in the group. As expected, the stock is down 18.2% since the results and currently trades at $18.35.

Libre 3 sensor correction: safety and reputation in the spotlight
-----------------------------------------------------------------

A second important overhang is the **safety correction** affecting Abbott’s continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) products.

On **November 24, 2025**, MedTech Dive reported that Abbott issued a **“medical device correction”** — not a formal recall — for around **3 million FreeStyle Libre 3 and Libre 3 Plus sensors** in the United States. The move followed reports that some sensors may deliver **falsely low glucose readings**, potentially leading users to overtreat with carbohydrates or reduce insulin unnecessarily. [[18]](https://www.medtechdive.com/news/abbott-libre-3-correction-accuracy/806345/?utm_source=ts2.tech)

Key data from Abbott’s communication, as reported: [[19]](https://www.medtechdive.com/news/abbott-libre-3-correction-accuracy/806345/?utm_source=ts2.tech)

*   **736 severe adverse events** and **7 deaths** worldwide associated with the affected sensors
*   In the **U.S.**, **57 severe adverse events** and **no deaths**
*   The problem is tied to **a single manufacturing line**, and roughly half of the affected sensors have already been used or expired
*   Abbott is offering **free replacement sensors** and does **not expect major supply disruptions**

The U.S. FDA had not yet listed the correction in its recall database as of the latest reporting, but the situation is being closely followed by regulators, physicians and patient groups. [[20]](https://www.medtechdive.com/news/abbott-libre-3-correction-accuracy/806345/?utm_source=ts2.tech)

The **Libre franchise** has been one of Abbott’s fastest‑growing product lines within Medical Devices, competing directly with Dexcom and Insulet in the booming CGM market. Any perceived reliability issues could: [[21]](https://www.medtechdive.com/news/abbott-libre-3-correction-accuracy/806345/?utm_source=ts2.tech)

*   Slow new patient uptake
*   Increase warranty or replacement costs
*   Heighten regulatory scrutiny and potential litigation risk

So far, the company’s messaging emphasizes that it has isolated the manufacturing issue and is proactively replacing affected sensors, but investors will watch for **any escalation into a formal recall or further adverse event disclosures**.

Risks to watch: litigation, integration and regulatory pressure
---------------------------------------------------------------

While the long‑term fundamentals appear solid, ABT is **not risk‑free**.

### 1. Deal execution and integration

The Exact Sciences acquisition must clear **regulatory and shareholder approvals**, and Abbott will then need to integrate a fast‑growing, R&D‑intensive oncology business without disrupting its culture or pipeline. Analysts note that **delays, divestiture requirements or integration missteps** could erode the high‑teens growth that makes Exact so attractive in the first place. [[35]](https://www.stocktitan.net/news/ABT/abbott-to-acquire-exact-sciences-a-leader-in-large-and-fast-growing-pvbv6z5xtczh.html?utm_source=ts2.tech)

### 2. Product safety and brand reputation

The Libre 3 correction underscores Abbott’s exposure to **device quality and safety risks**. Regulators have been tightening scrutiny on CGM systems, and any escalation — such as an FDA‑logged recall or more severe adverse‑event data — could pressure Libre’s growth and open the door wider for competitors. [[36]](https://www.medtechdive.com/news/abbott-libre-3-correction-accuracy/806345/?utm_source=ts2.tech)

### 3. Ongoing NEC baby formula litigation

Abbott also faces continuing **legal overhang** from lawsuits alleging that its **Similac** products contributed to **necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC)** in premature infants. A November 4, 2025 update from a plaintiffs’ law firm notes that around **755 cases remain pending in the federal MDL** (MDL 3026) alongside additional state‑court filings, with some early jury verdicts in related cases against other manufacturers reaching very large sums. [[37]](https://www.lawsuit-information-center.com/nec-baby-formula-lawsuits.html?utm_source=ts2.tech)

While allegations and verdicts are subject to appeals and do not automatically translate to Abbott outcomes, the litigation adds uncertainty around **potential future settlements, legal expenses and reputational impact**.

### 4. Macro and pricing pressures

Finally, Abbott is exposed to broader issues such as: [[38]](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/abbott-reports-third-quarter-2025-results-and-reaffirms-full-year-guidance-302584746.html?utm_source=ts2.tech)

*   **Foreign‑exchange volatility**, which can drag on reported international sales
*   **Volume‑based procurement and pricing reforms**, especially in China, affecting diagnostics
*   **Hospital capital‑spending cycles**, which can impact device orders and lab equipment upgrades

Management highlighted some of these pressures in explaining Q3 performance, even as it reaffirmed full‑year guidance.

Abbott Laboratories, together with its subsidiaries, discovers, develops, manufactures, and sells health care products worldwide. It operates in four segments: Established Pharmaceutical Products, Diagnostic Products, Nutritional Products, and Medical Devices. The company provides generic pharmaceuticals for the treatment of pancreatic exocrine insufficiency, irritable bowel syndrome or biliary spasm, intrahepatic cholestasis or depressive symptoms, gynecological disorder, hormone replacement therapy, dyslipidemia, hypertension, hypothyroidism, hypertriglyceridemia, Ménière's disease and vestibular vertigo, pain, fever, inflammation, and migraine, as well as provides anti-infective clarithromycin, influenza vaccine, and products to regulate physiological rhythm of the colon. It also offers laboratory and transfusion medicine systems in the areas of immunoassay, clinical chemistry, hematology, and transfusion serology testing; molecular diagnostics polymerase chain reaction instrument systems that automate the extraction, purification, and preparation of DNA and RNA from patient samples, and detect and measure infectious agents; point of care systems; cartridges for testing blood gas, chemistry, electrolytes, coagulation, and immunoassay; rapid diagnostics lateral flow testing products; molecular point-of-care testing for HIV, SARS-CoV-2, influenza A and B, RSV, and strep A; cardiometabolic test systems; and drug and alcohol test. In addition, the company provides pediatric and adult nutritional products and infant formula; rhythm management, electrophysiology, heart failure, vascular, and structural heart devices for the treatment of cardiovascular diseases; diabetes care products, such as glucose and blood glucose monitoring systems; and neuromodulation devices for the management of chronic pain and movement disorders. Abbott Laboratories was founded in 1888 and is based in North Chicago, Illinois.

-----------------------------------------------------

On **November 20, 2025**, Abbott announced a definitive agreement to acquire **Exact Sciences (NASDAQ: EXAS)**, a leading cancer screening and precision oncology company. *   Expand Cologuard and other tests internationally
*   Defend the franchise as blood‑based screening options gain traction

Libre 3 sensor correction: safety and reputation in the spotlight
-----------------------------------------------------------------

A second important overhang is the **safety correction** affecting Abbott’s continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) products.

On **November 24, 2025**, MedTech Dive reported that Abbott issued a **“medical device correction”** — not a formal recall — for around **3 million FreeStyle Libre 3 and Libre 3 Plus sensors** in the United States. The move followed reports that some sensors may deliver **falsely low glucose readings**, potentially leading users to overtreat with carbohydrates or reduce insulin unnecessarily. [[18]](https://www.medtechdive.com/news/abbott-libre-3-correction-accuracy/806345/?utm_source=ts2.tech)

Key data from Abbott’s communication, as reported: [[19]](https://www.medtechdive.com/news/abbott-libre-3-correction-accuracy/806345/?utm_source=ts2.tech)

*   **736 severe adverse events** and **7 deaths** worldwide associated with the affected sensors
*   In the **U.S.**, **57 severe adverse events** and **no deaths**
*   The problem is tied to **a single manufacturing line**, and roughly half of the affected sensors have already been used or expired
*   Abbott is offering **free replacement sensors** and does **not expect major supply disruptions**

The U.S. FDA had not yet listed the correction in its recall database as of the latest reporting, but the situation is being closely followed by regulators, physicians and patient groups. [[20]](https://www.medtechdive.com/news/abbott-libre-3-correction-accuracy/806345/?utm_source=ts2.tech)

The **Libre franchise** has been one of Abbott’s fastest‑growing product lines within Medical Devices, competing directly with Dexcom and Insulet in the booming CGM market. Any perceived reliability issues could: [[21]](https://www.medtechdive.com/news/abbott-libre-3-correction-accuracy/806345/?utm_source=ts2.tech)

*   Slow new patient uptake
*   Increase warranty or replacement costs
*   Heighten regulatory scrutiny and potential litigation risk

So far, the company’s messaging emphasizes that it has isolated the manufacturing issue and is proactively replacing affected sensors, but investors will watch for **any escalation into a formal recall or further adverse event disclosures**.

Risks to watch: litigation, integration and regulatory pressure
---------------------------------------------------------------

While the long‑term fundamentals appear solid, ABT is **not risk‑free**.

### 1. Deal execution and integration

The Exact Sciences acquisition must clear **regulatory and shareholder approvals**, and Abbott will then need to integrate a fast‑growing, R&D‑intensive oncology business without disrupting its culture or pipeline. Analysts note that **delays, divestiture requirements or integration missteps** could erode the high‑teens growth that makes Exact so attractive in the first place. [[35]](https://www.stocktitan.net/news/ABT/abbott-to-acquire-exact-sciences-a-leader-in-large-and-fast-growing-pvbv6z5xtczh.html?utm_source=ts2.tech)

### 2. Product safety and brand reputation

The Libre 3 correction underscores Abbott’s exposure to **device quality and safety risks**. Regulators have been tightening scrutiny on CGM systems, and any escalation — such as an FDA‑logged recall or more severe adverse‑event data — could pressure Libre’s growth and open the door wider for competitors. [[36]](https://www.medtechdive.com/news/abbott-libre-3-correction-accuracy/806345/?utm_source=ts2.tech)

### 3. Ongoing NEC baby formula litigation

Abbott also faces continuing **legal overhang** from lawsuits alleging that its **Similac** products contributed to **necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC)** in premature infants. A November 4, 2025 update from a plaintiffs’ law firm notes that around **755 cases remain pending in the federal MDL** (MDL 3026) alongside additional state‑court filings, with some early jury verdicts in related cases against other manufacturers reaching very large sums. [[37]](https://www.lawsuit-information-center.com/nec-baby-formula-lawsuits.html?utm_source=ts2.tech)

While allegations and verdicts are subject to appeals and do not automatically translate to Abbott outcomes, the litigation adds uncertainty around **potential future settlements, legal expenses and reputational impact**.

### 4. Macro and pricing pressures

Finally, Abbott is exposed to broader issues such as: [[38]](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/abbott-reports-third-quarter-2025-results-and-reaffirms-full-year-guidance-302584746.html?utm_source=ts2.tech)

*   **Foreign‑exchange volatility**, which can drag on reported international sales
*   **Volume‑based procurement and pricing reforms**, especially in China, affecting diagnostics
*   **Hospital capital‑spending cycles**, which can impact device orders and lab equipment upgrades

Management highlighted some of these pressures in explaining Q3 performance, even as it reaffirmed full‑year guidance.

Abbott Laboratories, together with its subsidiaries, discovers, develops, manufactures, and sells health care products worldwide. It operates in four segments: Established Pharmaceutical Products, Diagnostic Products, Nutritional Products, and Medical Devices. The company provides generic pharmaceuticals for the treatment of pancreatic exocrine insufficiency, irritable bowel syndrome or biliary spasm, intrahepatic cholestasis or depressive symptoms, gynecological disorder, hormone replacement therapy, dyslipidemia, hypertension, hypothyroidism, hypertriglyceridemia, Ménière's disease and vestibular vertigo, pain, fever, inflammation, and migraine, as well as provides anti-infective clarithromycin, influenza vaccine, and products to regulate physiological rhythm of the colon. It also offers laboratory and transfusion medicine systems in the areas of immunoassay, clinical chemistry, hematology, and transfusion serology testing; molecular diagnostics polymerase chain reaction instrument systems that automate the extraction, purification, and preparation of DNA and RNA from patient samples, and detect and measure infectious agents; point of care systems; cartridges for testing blood gas, chemistry, electrolytes, coagulation, and immunoassay; rapid diagnostics lateral flow testing products; molecular point-of-care testing for HIV, SARS-CoV-2, influenza A and B, RSV, and strep A; cardiometabolic test systems; and drug and alcohol test. In addition, the company provides pediatric and adult nutritional products and infant formula; rhythm management, electrophysiology, heart failure, vascular, and structural heart devices for the treatment of cardiovascular diseases; diabetes care products, such as glucose and blood glucose monitoring systems; and neuromodulation devices for the management of chronic pain and movement disorders. Abbott Laboratories was founded in 1888 and is based in North Chicago, Illinois.

# Q3 Earnings Outperformers: Abbott Laboratories (NYSE:ABT) And The Rest Of The Medical Devices & Supplies - Diversified Stocks

Adam Hejl

5 min read

In this article:  

[ABT

-0.72%](/quote/ABT/ "ABT")

Looking back on medical devices & supplies - diversified stocks’ Q3 earnings, we examine this quarter’s best and worst performers, including Abbott Laboratories (NYSE:ABT) and its peers.

The medical devices industry operates a business model that balances steady demand with significant investments in innovation and regulatory compliance. The industry benefits from recurring revenue streams tied to consumables, maintenance services, and incremental upgrades to the latest technologies. However, the capital-intensive nature of product development, coupled with lengthy regulatory pathways and the need for clinical validation, can weigh on profitability and timelines. In addition, there are constant pricing pressures from healthcare systems and insurers maximizing cost efficiency. Over the next several years, one tailwind is demographic–aging populations means rising chronic disease rates that drive greater demand for medical interventions and monitoring solutions. Advances in digital health, such as remote patient monitoring and smart devices, are also expected to unlock new demand by shortening upgrade cycles. On the other hand, the industry faces headwinds from pricing and reimbursement pressures as healthcare providers increasingly adopt value-based care models. Additionally, the integration of cybersecurity for connected devices adds further risk and complexity for device manufacturers.

The 5 medical devices & supplies - diversified stocks we track reported a mixed Q3. As a group, revenues beat analysts’ consensus estimates by 0.6% while next quarter’s revenue guidance was in line.

While some medical devices & supplies - diversified stocks have fared somewhat better than others, they have collectively declined. On average, share prices are down 4.3% since the latest earnings results.

## Abbott Laboratories (NYSE:ABT)

With roots dating back to 1888 when founder Dr. Wallace Abbott began producing precise, dosage-form medications, Abbott Laboratories (NYSE:ABT) develops and sells a diverse range of healthcare products including medical devices, diagnostics, nutrition products, and branded generic pharmaceuticals.

Abbott Laboratories reported revenues of $11.37 billion, up 6.9% year on year. This print was in line with analysts’ expectations, but overall, it was a mixed quarter for the company with organic revenue in line with analysts’ estimates.

"Our third-quarter results demonstrate our ability to deliver consistent, high-quality performance," said Robert B. Ford, chairman and chief executive officer, Abbott.

Unsurprisingly, the stock is down 7% since reporting and currently trades at $123.91.

## Best Q3: Neogen (NASDAQ:NEOG)

Founded in 1981 and operating at the intersection of food safety and animal health, Neogen (NASDAQ:NEOG) develops and manufactures diagnostic tests and related products to detect dangerous substances in food and pharmaceuticals for animal health.

Neogen reported revenues of $209.2 million, down 3.6% year on year, outperforming analysts’ expectations by 2.6%. The business had a very strong quarter with an impressive beat of analysts’ revenue estimates and full-year revenue guidance slightly topping analysts’ expectations.

Neogen achieved the biggest analyst estimates beat among its peers. The market seems happy with the results as the stock is up 7.9% since reporting. It currently trades at $6.28.

## Weakest Q3: Baxter (NYSE:BAX)

With a history dating back to 1931 and products used in over 100 countries, Baxter International (NYSE:BAX) provides essential healthcare products including dialysis therapies, IV solutions, infusion systems, surgical products, and patient monitoring technologies to hospitals and clinics worldwide.

Baxter reported revenues of $2.84 billion, up 5% year on year, falling short of analysts’ expectations by 1.4%. It was a softer quarter as it posted a significant miss of analysts’ full-year EPS guidance estimates and revenue guidance for next quarter missing analysts’ expectations significantly.

Baxter delivered the weakest performance against analyst estimates in the group. As expected, the stock is down 18.2% since the results and currently trades at $18.35.

Libre 3 sensor correction: safety and reputation in the spotlight
-----------------------------------------------------------------

A second important overhang is the **safety correction** affecting Abbott’s continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) products.

On **November 24, 2025**, MedTech Dive reported that Abbott issued a **“medical device correction”** — not a formal recall — for around **3 million FreeStyle Libre 3 and Libre 3 Plus sensors** in the United States. The move followed reports that some sensors may deliver **falsely low glucose readings**, potentially leading users to overtreat with carbohydrates or reduce insulin unnecessarily. [[18]](https://www.medtechdive.com/news/abbott-libre-3-correction-accuracy/806345/?utm_source=ts2.tech)

Key data from Abbott’s communication, as reported: [[19]](https://www.medtechdive.com/news/abbott-libre-3-correction-accuracy/806345/?utm_source=ts2.tech)

*   **736 severe adverse events** and **7 deaths** worldwide associated with the affected sensors
*   In the **U.S.**, **57 severe adverse events** and **no deaths**
*   The problem is tied to **a single manufacturing line**, and roughly half of the affected sensors have already been used or expired
*   Abbott is offering **free replacement sensors** and does **not expect major supply disruptions**

The U.S. FDA had not yet listed the correction in its recall database as of the latest reporting, but the situation is being closely followed by regulators, physicians and patient groups. [[20]](https://www.medtechdive.com/news/abbott-libre-3-correction-accuracy/806345/?utm_source=ts2.tech)

The **Libre franchise** has been one of Abbott’s fastest‑growing product lines within Medical Devices, competing directly with Dexcom and Insulet in the booming CGM market. Any perceived reliability issues could: [[21]](https://www.medtechdive.com/news/abbott-libre-3-correction-accuracy/806345/?utm_source=ts2.tech)

*   Slow new patient uptake
*   Increase warranty or replacement costs
*   Heighten regulatory scrutiny and potential litigation risk

So far, the company’s messaging emphasizes that it has isolated the manufacturing issue and is proactively replacing affected sensors, but investors will watch for **any escalation into a formal recall or further adverse event disclosures**.

Risks to watch: litigation, integration and regulatory pressure
---------------------------------------------------------------

While the long‑term fundamentals appear solid, ABT is **not risk‑free**.

### 1. Deal execution and integration

The Exact Sciences acquisition must clear **regulatory and shareholder approvals**, and Abbott will then need to integrate a fast‑growing, R&D‑intensive oncology business without disrupting its culture or pipeline. Analysts note that **delays, divestiture requirements or integration missteps** could erode the high‑teens growth that makes Exact so attractive in the first place. [[35]](https://www.stocktitan.net/news/ABT/abbott-to-acquire-exact-sciences-a-leader-in-large-and-fast-growing-pvbv6z5xtczh.html?utm_source=ts2.tech)

### 2. Product safety and brand reputation

The Libre 3 correction underscores Abbott’s exposure to **device quality and safety risks**. Regulators have been tightening scrutiny on CGM systems, and any escalation — such as an FDA‑logged recall or more severe adverse‑event data — could pressure Libre’s growth and open the door wider for competitors. [[36]](https://www.medtechdive.com/news/abbott-libre-3-correction-accuracy/806345/?utm_source=ts2.tech)

### 3. Ongoing NEC baby formula litigation

Abbott also faces continuing **legal overhang** from lawsuits alleging that its **Similac** products contributed to **necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC)** in premature infants. A November 4, 2025 update from a plaintiffs’ law firm notes that around **755 cases remain pending in the federal MDL** (MDL 3026) alongside additional state‑court filings, with some early jury verdicts in related cases against other manufacturers reaching very large sums. [[37]](https://www.lawsuit-information-center.com/nec-baby-formula-lawsuits.html?utm_source=ts2.tech)

While allegations and verdicts are subject to appeals and do not automatically translate to Abbott outcomes, the litigation adds uncertainty around **potential future settlements, legal expenses and reputational impact**.

### 4. Macro and pricing pressures

Finally, Abbott is exposed to broader issues such as: [[38]](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/abbott-reports-third-quarter-2025-results-and-reaffirms-full-year-guidance-302584746.html?utm_source=ts2.tech)

*   **Foreign‑exchange volatility**, which can drag on reported international sales
*   **Volume‑based procurement and pricing reforms**, especially in China, affecting diagnostics
*   **Hospital capital‑spending cycles**, which can impact device orders and lab equipment upgrades

Management highlighted some of these pressures in explaining Q3 performance, even as it reaffirmed full‑year guidance.

Abbott Laboratories, together with its subsidiaries, discovers, develops, manufactures, and sells health care products worldwide. It operates in four segments: Established Pharmaceutical Products, Diagnostic Products, Nutritional Products, and Medical Devices. The company provides generic pharmaceuticals for the treatment of pancreatic exocrine insufficiency, irritable bowel syndrome or biliary spasm, intrahepatic cholestasis or depressive symptoms, gynecological disorder, hormone replacement therapy, dyslipidemia, hypertension, hypothyroidism, hypertriglyceridemia, Ménière's disease and vestibular vertigo, pain, fever, inflammation, and migraine, as well as provides anti-infective clarithromycin, influenza vaccine, and products to regulate physiological rhythm of the colon. It also offers laboratory and transfusion medicine systems in the areas of immunoassay, clinical chemistry, hematology, and transfusion serology testing; molecular diagnostics polymerase chain reaction instrument systems that automate the extraction, purification, and preparation of DNA and RNA from patient samples, and detect and measure infectious agents; point of care systems; cartridges for testing blood gas, chemistry, electrolytes, coagulation, and immunoassay; rapid diagnostics lateral flow testing products; molecular point-of-care testing for HIV, SARS-CoV-2, influenza A and B, RSV, and strep A; cardiometabolic test systems; and drug and alcohol test. In addition, the company provides pediatric and adult nutritional products and infant formula; rhythm management, electrophysiology, heart failure, vascular, and structural heart devices for the treatment of cardiovascular diseases; diabetes care products, such as glucose and blood glucose monitoring systems; and neuromodulation devices for the management of chronic pain and movement disorders. Abbott Laboratories was founded in 1888 and is based in North Chicago, Illinois.

Abbott Laboratories, together with its subsidiaries, discovers, develops, manufactures, and sells health care products worldwide. It operates in four segments: Established Pharmaceutical Products, Diagnostic Products, Nutritional Products, and Medical Devices. The company provides generic pharmaceuticals for the treatment of pancreatic exocrine insufficiency, irritable bowel syndrome or biliary spasm, intrahepatic cholestasis or depressive symptoms, gynecological disorder, hormone replacement therapy, dyslipidemia, hypertension, hypothyroidism, hypertriglyceridemia, Ménière's disease and vestibular vertigo, pain, fever, inflammation, and migraine, as well as provides anti-infective clarithromycin, influenza vaccine, and products to regulate physiological rhythm of the colon. It also offers laboratory and transfusion medicine systems in the areas of immunoassay, clinical chemistry, hematology, and transfusion serology testing; molecular diagnostics polymerase chain reaction instrument systems that automate the extraction, purification, and preparation of DNA and RNA from patient samples, and detect and measure infectious agents; point of care systems; cartridges for testing blood gas, chemistry, electrolytes, coagulation, and immunoassay; rapid diagnostics lateral flow testing products; molecular point-of-care testing for HIV, SARS-CoV-2, influenza A and B, RSV, and strep A; cardiometabolic test systems; and drug and alcohol test. In addition, the company provides pediatric and adult nutritional products and infant formula; rhythm management, electrophysiology, heart failure, vascular, and structural heart devices for the treatment of cardiovascular diseases; diabetes care products, such as glucose and blood glucose monitoring systems; and neuromodulation devices for the management of chronic pain and movement disorders. Abbott Laboratories was founded in 1888 and is based in North Chicago, Illinois.

Abbott Laboratories, together with its subsidiaries, discovers, develops, manufactures, and sells health care products worldwide. It operates in four segments: Established Pharmaceutical Products, Diagnostic Products, Nutritional Products, and Medical Devices. The company provides generic pharmaceuticals for the treatment of pancreatic exocrine insufficiency, irritable bowel syndrome or biliary spasm, intrahepatic cholestasis or depressive symptoms, gynecological disorder, hormone replacement therapy, dyslipidemia, hypertension, hypothyroidism, hypertriglyceridemia, Ménière's disease and vestibular vertigo, pain, fever, inflammation, and migraine, as well as provides anti-infective clarithromycin, influenza vaccine, and products to regulate physiological rhythm of the colon. It also offers laboratory and transfusion medicine systems in the areas of immunoassay, clinical chemistry, hematology, and transfusion serology testing; molecular diagnostics polymerase chain reaction instrument systems that automate the extraction, purification, and preparation of DNA and RNA from patient samples, and detect and measure infectious agents; point of care systems; cartridges for testing blood gas, chemistry, electrolytes, coagulation, and immunoassay; rapid diagnostics lateral flow testing products; molecular point-of-care testing for HIV, SARS-CoV-2, influenza A and B, RSV, and strep A; cardiometabolic test systems; and drug and alcohol test. In addition, the company provides pediatric and adult nutritional products and infant formula; rhythm management, electrophysiology, heart failure, vascular, and structural heart devices for the treatment of cardiovascular diseases; diabetes care products, such as glucose and blood glucose monitoring systems; and neuromodulation devices for the management of chronic pain and movement disorders. Abbott Laboratories was founded in 1888 and is based in North Chicago, Illinois.

# Q3 Earnings Outperformers: Abbott Laboratories (NYSE:ABT) And The Rest Of The Medical Devices & Supplies - Diversified Stocks

Adam Hejl

5 min read

In this article:  

[ABT

-0.72%](/quote/ABT/ "ABT")

Looking back on medical devices & supplies - diversified stocks’ Q3 earnings, we examine this quarter’s best and worst performers, including Abbott Laboratories (NYSE:ABT) and its peers.

The medical devices industry operates a business model that balances steady demand with significant investments in innovation and regulatory compliance. The industry benefits from recurring revenue streams tied to consumables, maintenance services, and incremental upgrades to the latest technologies. However, the capital-intensive nature of product development, coupled with lengthy regulatory pathways and the need for clinical validation, can weigh on profitability and timelines. In addition, there are constant pricing pressures from healthcare systems and insurers maximizing cost efficiency. Over the next several years, one tailwind is demographic–aging populations means rising chronic disease rates that drive greater demand for medical interventions and monitoring solutions. **Abbott** (ABT) is one of the stocks most watched by Zacks.com visitors lately. So, it might be a good idea to review some of the factors that might affect the near-term performance of the stock.

Shares of this maker of infant formula, medical devices and drugs have returned +1.9% over the past month versus the Zacks S&P 500 composite's -0.6% change. The Zacks Medical - Products industry, to which Abbott belongs, has lost 1.1% over this period. Now the key question is: Where could the stock be headed in the near term?

While media releases or rumors about a substantial change in a company's business prospects usually make its stock 'trending' and lead to an immediate price change, there are always some fundamental facts that eventually dominate the buy-and-hold decision-making.

## Revisions to Earnings Estimates

Rather than focusing on anything else, we at Zacks prioritize evaluating the change in a company's earnings projection. This is because we believe the fair value for its stock is determined by the present value of its future stream of earnings.

Our analysis is essentially based on how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to take the latest business trends into account. When earnings estimates for a company go up, the fair value for its stock goes up as well. And when a stock's fair value is higher than its current market price, investors tend to buy the stock, resulting in its price moving upward. Because of this, empirical studies indicate a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and short-term stock price movements.

Abbott is expected to post earnings of $1.50 per share for the current quarter, representing a year-over-year change of +11.9%. Over the last 30 days, the Zacks Consensus Estimate remained unchanged.

The consensus earnings estimate of $5.15 for the current fiscal year indicates a year-over-year change of +10.3%. This estimate has remained unchanged over the last 30 days.

For the next fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $5.67 indicates a change of +10% from what Abbott is expected to report a year ago. Over the past month, the estimate has remained unchanged.

Having a strong externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool, the Zacks Rank, offers a more conclusive picture of a stock's price direction in the near term, since it effectively harnesses the power of earnings estimate revisions. Due to the size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, Abbott is rated Zacks Rank #3 (Hold).

## Projected Revenue Growth

While earnings growth is arguably the most superior indicator of a company's financial health, nothing happens as such if a business isn't able to grow its revenues. After all, it's nearly impossible for a company to increase its earnings for an extended period without increasing its revenues. So, it's important to know a company's potential revenue growth.

For Abbott, the consensus sales estimate for the current quarter of $11.79 billion indicates a year-over-year change of +7.5%. For the current and next fiscal years, $44.6 billion and $48.07 billion estimates indicate +6.3% and +7.8% changes, respectively.

## Last Reported Results and Surprise History

Abbott reported revenues of $11.37 billion in the last reported quarter, representing a year-over-year change of +6.9%. EPS of $1.3 for the same period compares with $1.21 a year ago.

Compared to the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $11.4 billion, the reported revenues represent a surprise of -0.23%. The EPS surprise was 0%.

Over the last four quarters, Abbott surpassed consensus EPS estimates two times. The company topped consensus revenue estimates just once over this period.

## Valuation

Without considering a stock's valuation, no investment decision can be efficient. In predicting a stock's future price performance, it's crucial to determine whether its current price correctly reflects the intrinsic value of the underlying business and the company's growth prospects.

Comparing the current value of a company's valuation multiples, such as its price-to-earnings (P/E), price-to-sales (P/S), and price-to-cash flow (P/CF), to its own historical values helps ascertain whether its stock is fairly valued, overvalued, or undervalued, whereas comparing the company relative to its peers on these parameters gives a good sense of how reasonable its stock price is.

The Zacks Value Style Score (part of the Zacks Style Scores system), which pays close attention to both traditional and unconventional valuation metrics to grade stocks from A to F (an A is better than a B; a B is better than a C; and so on), is pretty helpful in identifying whether a stock is overvalued, rightly valued, or temporarily undervalued.

Abbott is graded C on this front, indicating that it is trading at par with its peers. Click here to see the values of some of the valuation metrics that have driven this grade.

The facts discussed here and much other information on Zacks.com might help determine whether or not it's worthwhile paying attention to the market buzz about Abbott. However, its Zacks Rank #3 does suggest that it may perform in line with the broader market in the near term.

[[1]](https://markets.businessinsider.com/stocks/abt-stock?utm_source=ts2.tech)\\n\\nWith a market capitalization above **$220 billion** and membership in the S&P 500 Dividend Aristocrats index, Abbott remains a core holding for many income and healthcare-focused investors, meaning even relatively small headlines \u2013 like today\u2019s insider trade \u2013 can move the conversation around ABT stock. [[2]](https://markets.businessinsider.com/stocks/abt-stock?utm_source=ts2.tech)\\n\\n* * *\\n\\nAbbott Laboratories stock price snapshot for November 26, 2025\\n--------------------------------------------------------------\\n\\nAs of the latest completed trading session on **Tuesday, November 25**, Abbott Laboratories shares **closed at $128.06**, up **$0.84 (+0.66%)** from the prior close of $127.22. Intraday, the stock traded between **$126.24** and **$128.65**. [[3]](https://markets.businessinsider.com/stocks/abt-stock?utm_source=ts2.tech)\\n\\nOver the past year, ABT has traded in a **52\u2011week range of $110.81 to $141.16**, putting Tuesday\u2019s close roughly **9% below the 52\u2011week high** and about **16% above the low** \u2013 squarely in the middle of its yearly band. [[4]](https://markets.businessinsider.com/stocks/abt-stock?utm_source=ts2.tech)\\n\\nKey snapshot metrics at Tuesday\u2019s close include: [[5]](https://markets.businessinsider.com/stocks/abt-stock?utm_source=ts2.tech)\\n\\n*   **Market cap:** about **$223 billion**\\n*   **Shares outstanding:** ~1.74 billion\\n*   **Trailing EPS:** ~$7.64 per share\\n*   **Trailing P/E:** ~14.8x\\n*   **Annual dividend (trailing):** ~$2.24 per share\\n*   **Dividend yield:** just under **2%**\\n\\nData providers that adjust for non\u2011recurring items and use forward estimates generally place Abbott\u2019s **forward P/E in the low\u201120s**, a modest premium to the broader market but not extreme relative to high\u2011quality medtech peers. [[6]](https://www.directorstalkinterviews.com/abbott-laboratories-abt-stock-analysis-strong-buy-ratings-and-a-13-upside-potential/4121227029?utm_source=ts2.tech)\\n\\nSeparate performance trackers show Abbott up in the **high\u2011single digits over the last 12 months**, with a relatively steady climb in 2025 as healthcare and medtech names have come back into favor. [[7]](https://www.financecharts.com/stocks/ABT/summary/price?utm_source=ts2.tech)\\n\\n* * *\\n\\nFresh today: SVP Eric Shroff sells $203,000 in ABT stock\\n--------------------------------------------------------\\n\\nThe most immediate **November 26, 2025** news item for Abbott shareholders is an insider transaction:\\n\\n*   **Senior Vice President Eric Shroff** sold **1,586 shares** of Abbott common stock on **November 25, 2025**.\\n*   The shares were sold at prices between **$128.02 and $128.06**, for total proceeds of about **$203,042**. [[8]](https://in.investing.com/news/insider-trading-news/abbott-laboratories-svp-shroff-sells-203k-in-stock-93CH-5126650?utm_source=ts2.tech)\\n\\nAccording to the Form 4 filing, Shroff continues to own **30,384 Abbott shares** after the sale. [[9]](https://in.investing.com/news/insider-trading-news/abbott-laboratories-svp-shroff-sells-203k-in-stock-93CH-5126650?utm_source=ts2.tech)\\n\\nA related **Form 144** notice filed on November 25 clarifies that: [[10]](https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/ABT/144-abbott-laboratories-sec-filing-8c8f1a0e5bea.html?utm_source=ts2.tech)\\n\\n*   The **1,586 shares** derive from vested **restricted stock awards** that vested on **February 28, 2025** in three small tranches (740, 250 and 596 shares).\\n*   The notice lists an approximate sale date of **November 25, 2025** and references an aggregate market value of about **$203,042** for the shares.\\n*   The filing repeats the standard Rule 144 representation that the seller is **not aware of any undisclosed material adverse information** about Abbott\u2019s current or prospective operations.\\n\\nContext matters here: the planned sale of 1,586 shares is tiny compared with the **~1.74 billion shares outstanding** and comes from equity compensation rather than open\u2011market accumulation. StockTitan\u2019s AI\u2011generated summary flags the impact as **\u201cLow\u201d** and the sentiment as **\u201cNeutral.\u201d**[[11]](https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/ABT/144-abbott-laboratories-sec-filing-8c8f1a0e5bea.html?utm_source=ts2.tech)\\n\\nInsider sales like this are common at large, established companies and often reflect **portfolio diversification or tax planning**, not necessarily a negative view on the business. Still, traders sometimes treat clusters of insider selling as a short\u2011term sentiment indicator, so any follow\u2011on filings will be watched closely.\\n\\n* * *\\n\\nExact Sciences deal: a $21B bet on cancer diagnostics\\n-----------------------------------------------------\\n\\nBeyond today\u2019s insider headline, the **dominant story** for ABT in late November is its move into cancer diagnostics through a huge M&A deal.\\n\\nOn **November 20, 2025**, Abbott announced a definitive agreement to acquire **Exact Sciences (NASDAQ: EXAS)**, a leading cancer screening and precision oncology company. Key deal terms: [[12]](https://www.stocktitan.net/news/ABT/abbott-to-acquire-exact-sciences-a-leader-in-large-and-fast-growing-pvbv6z5xtczh.html?utm_source=ts2.tech)\\n\\n*   **Price:** $105 per EXAS share in cash\\n*   **Equity value:** approximately **$21 billion**\\n*   **Enterprise value:** about **$23 billion**, assuming ~**$1.8 billion** of Exact\u2019s net debt\\n*   **Expected closing:**Q2 2026, subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals\\n\\nExact Sciences is projected to generate **more than $3 billion in revenue in 2025**, with **high\u2011teens organic growth**, driven by a portfolio that includes: [[13]](https://www.stocktitan.net/news/ABT/abbott-to-acquire-exact-sciences-a-leader-in-large-and-fast-growing-pvbv6z5xtczh.html?utm_source=ts2.tech)\\n\\n*   **Cologuard\u00ae**, a non\u2011invasive stool\u2011based test for colorectal cancer screening\\n*   **Cologuard Plus**, a next\u2011generation version now rolling out\\n*   **Oncotype DX\u00ae**, which guides treatment decisions in breast cancer\\n*   Newer liquid\u2011biopsy offerings such as **Oncodetect\u2122** (molecular residual disease) and **Cancerguard\u2122** (multi\u2011cancer early detection)\\n\\nAbbott expects the acquisition to be **immediately accretive to revenue growth and gross margin**, and to push its diagnostics business above **$12 billion in annual sales**, giving it a major foothold in a **roughly $60 billion U.S. market** for cancer screening and precision oncology tests. [[14]](https://www.stocktitan.net/news/ABT/abbott-to-acquire-exact-sciences-a-leader-in-large-and-fast-growing-pvbv6z5xtczh.html?utm_source=ts2.tech)\\n\\nMarket reaction so far has been mixed:\\n\\n*   **Exact Sciences shares surged ~20\u201328%** on the deal speculation and subsequent announcement, reflecting the rich premium. [[15]](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/3216963/exact-sciences-exas-surges-on-potential-abbott-takeover?r=4bf001661e6fdd88d0cd7a5659ff9748&utm_campaign=headlines&utm_medium=syndication&utm_source=ts2.tech)\\n*   **Abbott shares initially fell around 2%** as investors digested the price tag and the added balance\u2011sheet risk, before stabilizing in the days that followed. [[16]](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/3216957/abbott-abt-shares-decline-amidst-takeover-speculation?mobile=true&utm_source=ts2.tech)\\n\\nAnalysts, including those cited by MedTech Dive and UBS, generally view the deal as **strategically smart**, giving Abbott a powerful growth engine to complement its diabetes, cardiovascular and core lab diagnostics franchises \u2013 but they also flag **integration and competitive risks**, especially as blood\u2011based cancer tests emerge from rivals. [[17]](https://www.medtechdive.com/news/abbott-exact-sciences-future-strategy/806178/?utm_source=ts2.tech)\\n\\nFor ABT shareholders, the **medium\u2011term stock narrative** is now tightly tied to whether Abbott can:\\n\\n*   Close the deal on schedule and on expected terms\\n*   Preserve Exact\u2019s innovation culture and scientific talent in Madison\\n*   Expand Cologuard and other tests internationally\\n*   Defend the franchise as blood\u2011based screening options gain traction\\n\\n* * *\\n\\nLibre 3 sensor correction: safety and reputation in the spotlight\\n-----------------------------------------------------------------\\n\\nA second important overhang is the **safety correction** affecting Abbott\u2019s continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) products.\\n\\nOn **November 24, 2025**, MedTech Dive reported that Abbott issued a **\u201cmedical device correction\u201d** \u2014 not a formal recall \u2014 for around **3 million FreeStyle Libre 3 and Libre 3 Plus sensors** in the United States. The move followed reports that some sensors may deliver **falsely low glucose readings**, potentially leading users to overtreat with carbohydrates or reduce insulin unnecessarily. [[18]](https://www.medtechdive.com/news/abbott-libre-3-correction-accuracy/806345/?utm_source=ts2.tech)\\n\\nKey data from Abbott\u2019s communication, as reported: [[19]](https://www.medtechdive.com/news/abbott-libre-3-correction-accuracy/806345/?utm_source=ts2.tech)\\n\\n*   **736 severe adverse events** and **7 deaths** worldwide associated with the affected sensors\\n*   In the **U.S.**, **57 severe adverse events** and **no deaths**\\n*   The problem is tied to **a single manufacturing line**, and roughly half of the affected sensors have already been used or expired\\n*   Abbott is offering **free replacement sensors** and does **not expect major supply disruptions**\\n\\nThe U.S. FDA had not yet listed the correction in its recall database as of the latest reporting, but the situation is being closely followed by regulators, physicians and patient groups. [[20]](https://www.medtechdive.com/news/abbott-libre-3-correction-accuracy/806345/?utm_source=ts2.tech)\\n\\nThe **Libre franchise** has been one of Abbott\u2019s fastest\u2011growing product lines within Medical Devices, competing directly with Dexcom and Insulet in the booming CGM market. Any perceived reliability issues could: [[21]](https://www.medtechdive.com/news/abbott-libre-3-correction-accuracy/806345/?utm_source=ts2.tech)\\n\\n*   Slow new patient uptake\\n*   Increase warranty or replacement costs\\n*   Heighten regulatory scrutiny and potential litigation risk\\n\\nSo far, the company\u2019s messaging emphasizes that it has isolated the manufacturing issue and is proactively replacing affected sensors, but investors will watch for **any escalation into a formal recall or further adverse event disclosures**.\\n\\n* * *\\n\\nEarnings, outlook and dividend: fundamentals underpin the story\\n---------------------------------------------------------------\\n\\nDespite these headlines, Abbott\u2019s **core operations remain healthy**.\\n\\nIn its **third\u2011quarter 2025** results released on October 15, Abbott reported: [[22]](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/abbott-reports-third-quarter-2025-results-and-reaffirms-full-year-guidance-302584746.html?utm_source=ts2.tech)\\n\\n*   **Reported sales growth:** 6.9% year over year\\n*   **Organic sales growth:** 5.5%, or **7.5% excluding COVID\u201119 testing**\\n*   **GAAP diluted EPS:** $0.94\\n*   **Adjusted diluted EPS:** $1.30\\n*   **Adjusted operating margin:** 23.0% of sales (up 40 bps)\\n\\nThe company **reaffirmed its full\u2011year 2025 guidance**, narrowing its adjusted EPS outlook to **$5.12\u2013$5.18**, which implies **double\u2011digit EPS growth at the midpoint**. [[23]](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/abbott-reports-third-quarter-2025-results-and-reaffirms-full-year-guidance-302584746.html?utm_source=ts2.tech)\\n\\nSegment highlights from the Q3 release include: [[24]](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/abbott-reports-third-quarter-2025-results-and-reaffirms-full-year-guidance-302584746.html?utm_source=ts2.tech)\\n\\n*   **Diagnostics:** Core lab revenue grew in the low\u2011single digits despite pricing and volume pressure in China.\\n*   **Medical Devices:** Continued strength in structural heart (MitraClip, TriClip) and diabetes care (Libre) drove mid\u2011 to high\u2011single\u2011digit growth.\\n*   **Nutrition:** International pediatric and adult nutrition remained a bright spot, while U.S. pediatric nutrition is still normalizing post\u2011infant\u2011formula disruptions.\\n*   **Established Pharmaceuticals:** Emerging\u2011markets branded generics delivered solid mid\u2011single\u2011digit growth on an organic basis.\\n\\nYear\u2011to\u2011date through Q3, Abbott\u2019s total sales are up just over **6% reported** and **6.4% organically** (or **7.7% excluding COVID testing**), broadly in line with management\u2019s long\u2011term ambition for **high\u2011single\u2011digit organic growth**. [[25]](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/abbott-reports-third-quarter-2025-results-and-reaffirms-full-year-guidance-302584746.html?utm_source=ts2.tech)\\n\\n### A classic dividend-growth story\\n\\nFor dividend investors, Abbott remains a **textbook dividend grower**:\\n\\n*   On **September 19, 2025**, the board declared its **407th consecutive quarterly dividend**, setting the payout at **$0.59 per share**, payable **November 17, 2025** to shareholders of record on **October 15, 2025**. [[26]](https://www.stocktitan.net/news/ABT/abbott-declares-407th-consecutive-quarterly-vo1qcmv8oi99.html?utm_source=ts2.tech)\\n*   Abbott has now **increased its dividend for 53 straight years**, placing it firmly in the **S&P 500 Dividend Aristocrats index**. [[27]](https://www.stocktitan.net/news/ABT/abbott-declares-407th-consecutive-quarterly-vo1qcmv8oi99.html?utm_source=ts2.tech)\\n*   Data from dividend trackers show Abbott\u2019s trailing 12\u2011month dividend at around **$2.24 per share**, with a **yield near 2%** at current prices. [[28]](https://markets.businessinsider.com/stocks/abt-stock?utm_source=ts2.tech)\\n\\nKiplinger\u2019s updated list of **\u201cBest Dividend Stocks to Buy for Dependable Dividend Growth\u201d** singles out Abbott for its **long history of annual increases**, noting that the company first paid a dividend in 1924 and has grown the payout for more than half a century, backed by a diverse portfolio that spans **Similac infant formula, Glucerna diabetes products and i\u2011Stat point\u2011of\u2011care diagnostic systems**. [[29]](https://www.kiplinger.com/investing/stocks/dividend-stocks/best-dividend-stocks-you-can-count-on?utm_source=ts2.tech)\\n\\nFor income\u2011oriented holders, the Exact Sciences deal and Libre 3 issues are important, but the **dividend track record and payout discipline** are key reasons many are willing to ride out short\u2011term volatility.\\n\\n* * *\\n\\nHow Wall Street sees ABT after the deal\\n---------------------------------------\\n\\nDespite the new risks, **Wall Street remains broadly bullish** on Abbott.\\n\\nMarkets Insider data show: [[30]](https://markets.businessinsider.com/stocks/abt-stock?utm_source=ts2.tech)\\n\\n*   **50 analysts** currently cover ABT\\n*   **46 rate it \u201cBuy\u201d**, 4 rate it \u201cHold,\u201d and **none rate it \u201cSell\u201d**\\n*   The **median 12\u2011month price target** is about **$139**, with a **range of $119\u2013$162**\\n\\nOther compilations of research coverage suggest even higher averages.
